title: Particle Markov chain Monte Carlo methods
notes: Source: journal-typeset PDF from A. Doucet's Oxford page; Journal of the Royal Statistical Society, Series B, 72(3):269-342 (2010), doi:10.1111/j.1467-9868.2009.00736.x. Authors: Christophe Andrieu, Arnaud Doucet, Roman Holenstein. 74 PDF pages: the read paper (Sections 1-5, Acknowledgements, Appendices A-B, References; printed pp. 269-302), then 'Discussion on the paper by Andrieu, Doucet and Holenstein' (contributions by many discussants), the authors' written reply, and 'References in the discussion'.

No TeX source exists: all mathematics, numbered equations (1)-(56) and many unnumbered displays, was transcribed to LaTeX from high-resolution page crops, with printed numbers as \tag. Equations (44)-(56) belong to the discussion. Equation (7) spans a page break: its tagged first line and the untagged continuation are consecutive blocks. Printed oddities are kept verbatim, e.g. 'Ocober' on the first page, q(·|...) without θ in step 2(b) of the SMC algorithm, product limits in (10), 'Section 4.5' for the particle Gibbs sampler, A versus A_0 in (18)-(19), p_θ(x_n|y_n, x_n) in Section 3.1, q_1(·) in conditional SMC step 1(a), the duplicated '∈ X^n ∈ X^n' in the definition of S_n^θ, X_{1:T} in Theorem 6(a), 'equation (8)' and 'unormalized' in Section 4.5, {K} in the display of B.4, a missing parenthesis in (47), U_{n-1} without tilde in (53), W_T^{*K} in (56).

The algorithm descriptions (SMC, PIMH, PMMH, conditional SMC, particle Gibbs, and the discussants' algorithms) are printed as step lists and kept as text, one paragraph per printed step. Theorems 1-6, Assumptions 1-7, Propositions and Lemmas carry bold printed labels.

Discussion: each contribution has a heading '<Name> (<affiliation>)' as printed; the authors' reply is under 'The authors replied later, in writing, as follows', with its italic topic titles as italic lines. Figures 1-7 belong to the paper (assets figure-1..figure-7); Figures 8-23 and the tables of the discussion have assets named with a 'd' and the PDF page (e.g. figure-d8-p0035, table-d1-p0040, table-d-p0039 for an unnumbered table). Figures 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 are printed sideways and kept in page orientation. Line-style samples printed inside captions as legend marks are approximated with characters.

Full-page figures that interrupt a running paragraph (Figs 5, 6-7, 9-10, 17) are placed after the paragraph that continues across them; Fig. 19 (printed on a full page inside the next contribution) and Fig. 20 (printed on the preceding page) are placed inside the contributions that cite them (Lee and Holmes; Yun and Chen); other floats sit at paragraph boundaries near their printed position. The first-page footer (address for correspondence, copyright and journal lines) precedes Section 1. In places the journal prints the digit 1 with a glyph identical to the letter 'l' (e.g. '(l999)', 'AR(l)', 'PIMH-Reusel'), and the PDF text layer stores it as 'l'; it is written as the digit 1 here.
source_review_notes: All 74 pages reviewed against page renders by eight reviewer agents (pages 1-9, 10-18, 19-27, 28-36, 37-46, 47-56, 57-65, 66-74; reports/review-pages-*.md): mathematics transcribed from 200-330 dpi crops, 23 figures re-boxed, discussion tables transcribed, both reference lists rebuilt one entry per item, joins set across pages. Remaining verifier diagnostics are LaTeX-notation differences, U+2212 minus glyphs, caption legend marks, and l/1 glyph confusions in the text layer, adjudicated per page.
